title: Topology filter — services and routes filter by operator
preface: This test is to confirm that services and routes can be filtered and managed by operator level within the CloudFare Operator Hierarchy.
preconds:
**GIVEN** the user is in the Topology & Fares Management module
**AND** more than one operator level exists in the CloudFare Operator Hierarchy

steps.content: **WHEN** the user selects an operator level in the hierarchy
steps.expected:
**THEN** only that level's services and routes are shown
**UNCONFIRMED** — no discrete 'filter by operator' control is described; confirm the actual live control

change_note: Relocated the inline FBD paragraph citations (previously baked into the UNCONFIRMED sentence) to Refs; shortened the marker to a tag per the terse mandate. Behaviour/gap substance unchanged.
gaps: No discrete 'filter by operator' UI control is described in the governing specs — only an Operator Hierarchy level (FBD-100385 para 178) and a fixed OperatorId of 1 (FBD-100698 para 86). Confirm the exact live control.

title: Fares export — configured fares are exported

**GIVEN** the user is signed into CloudFare
**AND** routes with a shared Service Group have fares configured (e.g. routes sharing one service group)

steps.content: **WHEN** the user runs the fares export (Fares Export function, or exports fares for routes sharing a Service Group)
steps.expected:
**THEN** the fares file is produced
**UNCONFIRMED** — the export surface/parameters are not confirmed; confirm live

change_note: Relocated inline FBD citations to Refs; shortened marker text. No behavioural change.
gaps: Governing specs place fares export in the Reports module / a dedicated Fares Export function (FBD-100385 para 157-159, detailed in FBD-100336) and describe export for routes sharing a Service Group (FBD-100296 para 241); export 'for a selected operator' from the Topology & Fares page is not confirmed. Confirm the surface and parameters live.

title: Route Management — create, amend, copy and delete a route
preface: This test is to confirm the user can create, amend, copy and delete a route in the Route Management module. Note: this bundles four behaviours; consider splitting per the Gherkin standard.
preconds: **GIVEN** the user is in the Route Management module with a Service selected in the Services sub-module

steps.content: **WHEN** the user presses 'Create New Route' in the Routes sub-module, completes the route attributes and stops, and presses 'Add Route'
steps.expected: **THEN** the new route is added and appears in the Routes drop-down

steps.content: **WHEN** the user selects the route, opens the '3 dot' menu on the Route Pane and chooses 'Edit Route Attributes' (or 'Copy Route', or 'Delete Route')
steps.expected:
**THEN** 'Edit Route Attributes' applies the amended attributes
**AND** 'Copy Route' creates a copy in the same Service named '<route>-copy'
**AND** 'Delete Route' removes the route after the Yes/No confirmation
**UNCONFIRMED** — that a copy retains its fare area is not confirmed; verify against the fares spec/live

change_note: Relocated inline FBD citation to Refs; shortened marker. No behavioural change.
gaps: That a copied route 'retains its assigned fare area' is not in FBD-100296 (fares are explicitly out of scope of that spec, para 44); confirm fare-area copy behaviour against the fares spec/live.

steps.expected:
**THEN** the route is saved with the selected Service and Public Route Code
**UNCONFIRMED** — no per-route 'service code'/'operator' field exists in the spec; confirm the live screen's terms

change_note: Relocated inline FBD citation to Refs; shortened marker. Flagged title/expected-result drift for the engineer.
gaps: FBD-100296 route attributes are 'Add to a Service' and 'Public Route Code' (para 236-238); there is no per-route 'service code' field nor a per-route 'operator' assignment (routes belong to a Service, not an operator). The case title and the Expected-result summary still say 'service code' and 'operator' — confirm what those terms map to on the live screen, and consider retitling to match the real field names.
